followup_reviews.Separate challenger: GPT-6 Astra Pro /root/verification_recovery, separate same-model context
followup_reviews.Research finding: Two distinct Tompa–Kelebia interruptions are supported and remain included; the separate 8 February event is not joined to 6–7 February. P1 is road-crossing processing as described by police. P2 is only freight entering Hungary, while passenger movement in both directions and outbound freight continued. P1 starts 6 February 2020 at 16:00 and ends a few minutes after 7 February 07:00: about 15 hours, with a one-day calendar-date difference and unknown exact reopening minute. P2 is 8 February 10:30–11:16, 46 minutes, retained as same-day with no whole-day duration. Police cited safe/unobstructed crossing and security. Migrant presence is contextual; an additional unreported political motive is not inferred. The 24.hu report and MKFE notice share the same county-police origin. The 8 February primary police statement was directly read. These are source checks, not three independent witnesses. Both phases are currently unlocated. A narrower inbound freight gate on 8 February must not inherit an all-traffic geometry or a whole Hungary–Serbia frontier closure.
followup_reviews.Challenge verdict: Accepted within the root decision; see frozen challenge

Apply the challenger’s medical-visa cohort, shared-reporting inference and unread-translation metadata refinements. Unknown dates, continuity, exceptions, missing source access and geographic limits remain explicit. This is a completed audit procedure for the sample, not a certification that all attributes are known or that the full register has been freshly verified.
